# NOW — the Chronicle

**BOOK I — THE HOUSE OF MENDERS · Chapter 4 — Old Mercy · the noon bell and after, two days after Old Mercy was said**

- **Where:** Saint Ysolde's, the House of Menders; the cloister, in a plain chair facing Hollis's across a sword's length of wet flags, the kitchen in its door, Wren on the fountain's rim, Ash in the arcade.
- **The quest:** *The List.* The Confessors have come for the Faithless at Saint Ysolde's with a list: Darrow first, Hollis second. What stands between them and the hall is Old Mercy, the sanctuary bell: while it rings at dawn and dusk, no blade passes the gate and no name under it is taken down against its will. Marrant has not drawn a blade in a month. He has camped on the lower terrace, kept the cage, and reached into the House by the lever: a clerk in grey who never kneels sent two black slivers up in the House's own letter-satchel, one of them now set in the rock under the row and making the stone grow frost, and holds the almoner's sister at Calden for the second. Banners that are not grey are on the Holloway, a day off.
- **What Darrow is fighting right now:** The false letter is written and held: the second set, the hall quiet, in the almoner's own hand with every word's purpose told, and in it a brother's questions for his sister, where she is kept and a line in her hand, and one true line. It goes down with the carter and is read at the winch-house. If it is believed, the Confessor waits and the clerk may name the place; if it is caught, the next letter up comes without her mark. The answer at the dawn bell is owed under the Prior's roof.
- **Just happened (Scene):** *Sitting Down.* "Hit me properly. Once. So I know what you've got." The kitchen went quiet. Wren's pencil stopped.
- **With him:** Maelis Vorne (Gone back up from the kennels. She has seen the Captain's hand go to the drain grate and come away; since *The Lymer*) · Ser Hollis Garrow (In his chair in the cloister with the wooden sword across his knees, winded and steady-eyed, having asked the Captain to hit him properly, once, so he knows what he has.) · Wren Ashdown (On the fountain's rim in the cloister with her pencil stopped.) · Ash (In the cloister near the Captain's chair, the bone left in the arcade.)
- **Also here:** Ser Aldric Vane (Wrote again from Calden, before the list was read: Calden says the Ninth broke faith when its captain turned out of the line for one of his…) · Ser Benedek Orrin (Said his oath at the noon bell with Hollis's hand round his; the frost on his mouth neither grew nor melted.) · Brother Anselm (Was on the next cot in the morning as he had been told, the key on its cord and the letter inside his shirt, waiting on the carter.) · Brother Cobb (Sat on a keg in the forge door taking the inside of Hollis's leather cup down a shaving at a time; told the Captain he was in his light and…) · Confessor Ivo Marrant (Stood behind his men's lymer on the terrace path below the kennels, said the hound was learning the House so it would know it again on the…) · Mother Ione (Came out of the chapel unasked and stood beside the Captain under the tower while he said the verse, then at the bars; told the Confessor t…) · Sister Pell (Came down the row between the dawn bell and the hour bell; read the Captain's mouth and made him say it plain; refused her hands with Ask t…)
- **The tales:** Tale 1 — Quickstep (1 of 3 told) · Tale 2 — Road's the Road (told in full)
- **Against him:** Marrant has his answer from under the Prior's roof and a lymer learning the House for the road; the almoner's letter waits inside his shirt for the carter, to be read at the winch-house like every letter now; the cold comes up through the kennel grate; one sliver is in the wall under the row, the other in Maelis's coat; one grey cloak has gone down the Steps with a horse; the banners on the Holloway are a day off.
- **Next:** A man in a chair has asked to be hit properly.
- **Open choice:** none.
